primitives.name: Ecological Dynamics
primitives.verbatim_quote: An Ecological Dynamics theoretical framework for understanding performance, learning and development in football.
primitives.assumptions: Non-linear interactions between player, teammates, opponents, and environmental constraints.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when environmental constraints become too rigid or chaotic.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Maps to conformal predictive regions for player performance distributions. GSE: Models state-transitions in game dynamics via attractor basins.
layer2.telemetry: Measures coordination patterns and stability transitions in player movement data.

primitives.name: Dynamical Transactions
primitives.verbatim_quote: There is a special emphasis on the dynamical transactions that emerge between players, coaches and support staff with the performance contexts of this team sport.
primitives.assumptions: Coupled oscillators model mutual influence between actors; linear approximations fail near bifurcation points.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Bifurcations occur when transaction intensity exceeds system capacity, leading to cascading failures.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Maps to Bayesian network updates reflecting information flow between agents. GSE: Represents belief-state transitions in multi-agent reinforcement learning.
layer2.telemetry: Tracks temporal correlations in decision-making lags and response times across the team.

primitives.name: Skill Acquisition
primitives.verbatim_quote: This book focuses on how skills are learned, as expertise and knowledge of the competitive environment in football are refined through practice and experience.
primitives.assumptions: Learning is a self-organizing process driven by sensory-motor coupling; error reduction is secondary to behavioral variability.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Overtraining leads to loss of flexibility, causing rigid control and vulnerability to unexpected perturbations.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Maps to sequential Monte Carlo filters tracking evolving skill proficiency over time. GSE: Encodes skill as transition probabilities between game states.
layer2.telemetry: Quantifies changes in movement entropy and coordination variance during training sessions.

primitives.name: Motor Learning
primitives.verbatim_quote: To achieve these aims, the book draws upon the psychological study of human behaviour, especially in the applied scientific domain of motor learning.
primitives.assumptions: Behavioral change is governed by internal models and forward predictions; adaptation occurs through prediction-error minimization.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Model mismatch causes instability; optimal adaptation rate balances exploration and exploitation.

layer2.mapping: GSI: Maps to Kalman filter-based tracking of latent motor states. GSE: Represents learning as updates in policy gradients within Markov decision processes.
layer2.telemetry: Monitors prediction-error signals from brain activity and movement kinematics.
